name: Facto-DSA
full_name: Cubic Factorisation Based Multivariate Digital Signature Algorithm

overview_classification.summary_label_zh: 多变量密码 / 三次因式分解型签名

hardness_problems.name: Facto-DSA public inversion
hardness_problems.details: Inverting the published dense homogeneous cubic map

hardness_problems.name: Facto-DSA trapdoor recovery
hardness_problems.details: Recovering equivalent hidden input/output maps and triangular quadratic structure

hardness_problems.name: polynomial factorisation with bounded split
hardness_problems.details: Signer factors completed target polynomial and inverts a hidden triangular quadratic map

mathematical_structures: homogeneous cubic polynomial systems over F_65519

common_parameters.central_map: (X,Y) -> (Q(X)+R(Y))*Y followed by hidden input maps and output projection
hash_xof_prg: domain-separated message hash with public-key digest

expected_repetitions.Facto-DSA-128: at most about 1/0.26 from the conservative lower bound
expected_repetitions.Facto-DSA-256: at most about 1/0.22 from the conservative lower bound
expected_repetitions.Facto-DSA-512: at most about 1/0.19 from the conservative lower bound

signing_behavior.notes: Per-set retry limits are stored in parameters as Rmax=512/1024/2048; schema has only one common retry_limit field.

security_claims.claim: Submission claims classical EUF-CMA under the Facto-DSA public-inversion assumption with bad-event terms for signing failure and hash collisions.
Submission states a QROM analogue with quantum random-oracle query losses.

claimed_advantages.summary: Produces exceptionally short fixed signatures of 40, 68 and 128 bytes.
Uses linear, polynomial and modular algebra and a portable ISO C interface without external libraries.
Parameters n, m, output-minus dimension and retry bound can be adjusted for new cost data.
Provides portable, performance-optimized and resource-optimized versions across x86-64, ARM and RISC-V.

limitations_and_constraints.summary: Dense cubic public keys range from 40,040 bytes to 5,674,240 bytes and dominate transmission when sent with a message.
Signing is probabilistic and capped at 512/1024/2048 trials, with claimed failure below 2^-222/2^-367/2^-622.
Security depends on a new cubic factorisation-based public inversion/trapdoor-recovery assumption following attacks on earlier quadratic factorisation schemes.
Performance tables cover specific x86-64, ARM and RISC-V systems and multiple implementation profiles.

sources.notes: Basic-information form embedded as appendix in specification and separately supplied.
